subject: 2D change point detection with Cauchy distribution

messages.author: 55d1a09c85eadab7
messages.subject: 2D change point detection with Cauchy distribution
parts:
Hi,

I can detect 1D change points with Cauchy distribution (e.g. model-1d.stan, run-1d.R, fig-1d.png).

But, I have no idea how to construct mu in transformed parameters block in the 2D case (e.g. generate-2d.R, fig-2d.png), because mu[i,j] <- mu[i,j-1] + s_mu*tan(mu_unif[i,j-1]) and mu[i,j] <- mu[i-1,j] + s_mu*tan(mu_unif[i-1,j]) come into collision.  Do you have any good idea?

Regards,
Bee

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] 2D change point detection with Cauchy distribution
parts:
I'm not sure waht a 2D change point is.

If you want to follow what I did in the manual for the
minining disasters example (and note that Andrew isn't keen
on these discrete changepoint models --- it was just an example
to show that we could do it), then you need to decide how to
model the mixture. The diagram makes it look like a 2D rectangle
in a bigger rectangle. If it's any shape and size of rectangle,
then I think that gives you O(N^3) mixture components to evaluate
each iteration. But otherwise, you do it exactly the same way.

- Bob
